shloka_text: श्रुत्वागस्त्येरितं वाक्यं रामो विस्मयमागतः । कथमासीत्तु लङ्कायां सम्भवो रक्षसां पुरा ।। 7.4.1 ।।
transliteration: śrutvāgastyeritaṃ vākyaṃ rāmo vismayamāgataḥ | kathamāsīttu laṅkāyāṃ sambhavo rakṣasāṃ purā || 7.4.1 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, अगस्त्येरितं spoken by Agastya, वाक्यं statement, रामः Rama, विस्मयमागतः became astonished, कथं how, आसीत् was, तु indeed, लङ्कायां in Lanka, सम्भवः origin, रक्षसां of Rakshasas, पुरा formerly.
explanation: Having heard the words spoken by Agastya, Rama was filled with astonishment, wondering how the Rakshasas could have originated in Lanka in ancient times.
comments: At Rama's wonder over the earlier rakshasas, Agastya tells how Brahma, having created the waters, made beings to guard them -- those who cried 'we will guard' became rakshasas and those 'we will eat' became yakshas -- of the line of Heti and Praheti: Heti weds Bhaya, sister of Death, and begets Vidyutkesha, whose abandoned son is saved and made immortal by Shiva and Parvati as Sukesha, granted a sky-faring city.

shloka_text: ततः शिरः कम्पयित्वा त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम् । तमगस्त्यं मुहुर्दृष्ट्वा स्मयमानो ऽभ्यभाषत ।। 7.4.2 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śiraḥ kampayitvā tretāgnisamavigraham | tamagastyaṃ muhurdṛṣṭvā smayamāno 'bhyabhāṣata || 7.4.2 ||
translation: ततः then, शिरः head, कम्पयित्वा having shaken, त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहम् whose body was like the three sacred fires, तम् him, अगस्त्यं Agastya, मुहुः repeatedly, दृष्ट्वा having seen, स्मयमानः smiling, अभ्यभाषत spoke to.
explanation: Then, shaking his head and repeatedly looking at Agastya, whose body resembled the three sacred fires, Rama smiled and spoke to him.

shloka_text: भगवन्पूर्वमप्येषा लङ्कासीत्पिशिताशिनाम् । श्रुत्वेदं भगवद्वाक्यं जातो मे विस्मयः परः ।। 7.4.3 ।।
transliteration: bhagavanpūrvamapyeṣā laṅkāsītpiśitāśinām | śrutvedaṃ bhagavadvākyaṃ jāto me vismayaḥ paraḥ || 7.4.3 ||
translation: भगवन् O revered one, पूर्वम् formerly, अपि even, एषा this, लङ्का Lanka, आसीत् was, पिशिताशिनाम् of flesh-eaters, श्रुत्वा having heard, इदं this, भगवद्वाक्यं your revered statement, जातः arisen, मे my, विस्मयः astonishment, परः great.
explanation: O revered one, having heard your statement that this Lanka formerly belonged to the flesh-eaters, a great astonishment has arisen within me.

shloka_text: पुलस्त्यवंशादुद्भूता राक्षसा इति नः श्रुतम् । इदानीमन्यतश्चापि सम्भवः कीर्तितस्त्वया ।। 7.4.4 ।।
transliteration: pulastyavaṃśādudbhūtā rākṣasā iti naḥ śrutam | idānīmanyataścāpi sambhavaḥ kīrtitastvayā || 7.4.4 ||
translation: पुलस्त्यवंशात् from Pulastya's lineage, उद्भूताः originated, राक्षसाः Rākṣasas, इति thus, नः by us, श्रुतम् heard, इदानीम् now, अन्यतः from another source, च and, अपि also, सम्भवः origin, कीर्तितः narrated, त्वया by you.
explanation: We have heard that the Rākṣasas originated from Pulastya's lineage, but now you have also spoken of their origin from another source.

shloka_text: रावणात्कुम्भकर्णाच्च प्रहस्ताद्विकटादपि । रावणस्य च पुत्रेभ्यः किं नु ते बलवत्तराः ।। 7.4.5 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇātkumbhakarṇācca prahastādvikaṭādapi | rāvaṇasya ca putrebhyaḥ kiṃ nu te balavattarāḥ || 7.4.5 ||
translation: रावणात् than Rāvaṇa, कुम्भकर्णात् than Kumbhakarṇa, च and, प्रहस्तात् than Prahasta, विकटात् than Vikaṭa, अपि even, रावणस्य of Rāvaṇa, च and, पुत्रेभ्यः than the sons, किम् what, नु indeed, ते they, बलवत्तराः more powerful.
explanation: Are these new Rākṣasas indeed more powerful than Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Prahasta, Vikaṭa, and even Rāvaṇa's own sons?

shloka_text: क एषां पूर्वको ब्रह्मन्किन्नामा च बलोत्कटः । अपराधं च कं प्राप्य विष्णुना द्राविताः कथम् ।। 7.4.6 ।।
transliteration: ka eṣāṃ pūrvako brahmankinnāmā ca balotkaṭaḥ | aparādhaṃ ca kaṃ prāpya viṣṇunā drāvitāḥ katham || 7.4.6 ||
translation: कः who, एषाम् among them, पूर्वकः the first/ancestor, ब्रह्मन् O Brāhmaṇa, किन्नामा what name, च and, बलोत्कटः exceedingly powerful, अपराधम् offense, च and, कम् what, प्राप्य having committed, विष्णुना by Viṣṇu, द्राविताः driven away/destroyed, कथम् how.
explanation: O Brāhmaṇa, who was their first ancestor, what was his name, and how were these exceedingly powerful beings driven away by Viṣṇu after committing what offense?

shloka_text: एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ । कुतूहलमिदं मह्यं नुद भानुर्यथा तमः ।। 7.4.7 ।।
transliteration: etadvistarataḥ sarvaṃ kathayasva mamānagha | kutūhalamidaṃ mahyaṃ nuda bhānuryathā tamaḥ || 7.4.7 ||
translation: एतत् this, विस्तरतः in detail, सर्वम् all, कथयस्व please narrate, मम to me, अनघ O sinless one, कुतूहलम् curiosity, इदम् this, मह्यम् my, नुद dispel, भानुः the sun, यथा just as, तमः darkness.
explanation: O sinless one, please narrate all of this to me in detail and dispel my great curiosity, just as the sun dispels darkness.

shloka_text: राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संस्कारालङ्कृतं शुभम् । ईषद्विस्मयमानस्तमगस्त्यः प्राह राघवम् ।। 7.4.8 ।।
transliteration: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃskārālaṅkṛtaṃ śubham | īṣadvismayamānastamagastyaḥ prāha rāghavam || 7.4.8 ||
translation: राघवस्य of Rāghava, वचः words, श्रुत्वा having heard, संस्कारालङ्कृतम् adorned with refinement, शुभम् auspicious/beautiful, ईषत् slightly, विस्मयमानः being surprised, तम् him, अगस्त्यः Agastya, प्राह said, राघवम् to Rāghava.
explanation: Having heard Rāghava's auspicious words, adorned with refinement, Agastya, slightly surprised, spoke to Rāghava.

shloka_text: प्रजापतिः पुरा सृष्ट्वा ह्यपः सलिलसम्भवः । तासां गोपायने सत्त्वानसृजत्पद्मसम्भवः ।। 7.4.9 ।।
transliteration: prajāpatiḥ purā sṛṣṭvā hyapaḥ salilasambhavaḥ | tāsāṃ gopāyane sattvānasṛjatpadmasambhavaḥ || 7.4.9 ||
translation: प्रजापतिः Prajapati, पुरा formerly, सृष्ट्वा having created, हि indeed, अपः waters, सलिलसम्भवः born from water, तासाम् of those (waters), गोपायने for the protection, सत्त्वान् beings, असृजत् created, पद्मसम्भवः born from a lotus.
explanation: In ancient times, Prajapati Brahma, who was born from water and a lotus, first created the waters and then created various beings for their protection.

shloka_text: ते सत्त्वाः सत्त्वकर्तारं विनीतवदुपस्थिताः । किं कुर्म इति भाषन्तः क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः ।। 7.4.10 ।।
transliteration: te sattvāḥ sattvakartāraṃ vinītavadupasthitāḥ | kiṃ kurma iti bhāṣantaḥ kṣutpipāsābhayārditāḥ || 7.4.10 ||
translation: ते those, सत्त्वाः beings, सत्त्वकर्तारम् to the creator of beings, विनीतवत् humbly, उपस्थिताः stood before, किम् what, कुर्मः shall we do, इति thus, भाषन्तः speaking, क्षुत्पिपासाभयार्दिताः afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear.
explanation: Those beings, afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fear, humbly approached their creator and asked, "What shall we do?"

shloka_text: प्रजापतिस्तु तान्याह सत्वानि प्रहसन्निव । आभाष्य वाचा यत्नेन रक्षध्वमिति मानदः ।। 7.4.11 ।।
transliteration: prajāpatistu tānyāha satvāni prahasanniva | ābhāṣya vācā yatnena rakṣadhvamiti mānadaḥ || 7.4.11 ||
translation: प्रजापतिः Prajapati, तु indeed, तान् to them, आह said, सत्त्वानि to the beings, प्रहसन् as if laughing, इव as it were, आभाष्य having addressed, वाचा with words, यत्नेन with effort, रक्षध्वम् protect, इति thus, मानदः the giver of honor.
explanation: Prajapati, the giver of honor, addressed those beings as if with a smile and instructed them with effort, "Protect!"

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च तत्रान्ये जक्षाम इति चापरे । भुक्षिताभुक्षितैरुक्तस्ततस्तानाह भूतकृत् ।। 7.4.12 ।।
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca tatrānye jakṣāma iti cāpare | bhukṣitābhukṣitairuktastatastānāha bhūtakṛt || 7.4.12 ||
translation: रक्षाम we will protect, इति thus, च and, तत्र among them, अन्ये others, जक्षाम we will eat, इति thus, च and, अपरे others, भुक्षिताभुक्षितैः by those who desired to eat and those who did not desire to eat, उक्तः having been spoken to, ततः then, तान् to them, आह said, भूतकृत् the creator of beings.
explanation: Among those beings, some said, "We will protect," while others said, "We will eat"; then, having heard these responses from the hungry and the non-hungry, the creator of beings spoke to them.

shloka_text: रक्षामेति च यैरुक्तं राक्षसास्ते भवन्तु वः । जक्षाम इति यैरुक्तं यक्षा एव भवन्तु वः ।। 7.4.13 ।।
transliteration: rakṣāmeti ca yairuktaṃ rākṣasāste bhavantu vaḥ | jakṣāma iti yairuktaṃ yakṣā eva bhavantu vaḥ || 7.4.13 ||
translation: रक्षाम we will protect, इति thus, च and, यैः by whom, उक्तम् was said, राक्षसाः Rakshasas, ते those, भवन्तु let them be, वः you. जक्षाम we will eat, इति thus, यैः by whom, उक्तम् was said, यक्षाः Yakshas, एव indeed, भवन्तु let them be, वः you.
explanation: To those who said, "We will protect," he declared, "You shall be Rakshasas," and to those who said, "We will eat," he declared, "You shall indeed be Yakshas."

shloka_text: तत्र हेतिः प्रहेतिश्च भ्रातरौ राक्षसाधिपौ । मधुकैटभसङ्काशौ बभूवतुररिन्दमौ ।। 7.4.14 ।।
transliteration: tatra hetiḥ prahetiśca bhrātarau rākṣasādhipau | madhukaiṭabhasaṅkāśau babhūvaturarindamau || 7.4.14 ||
translation: तत्र there, हेतिः Heti, प्रहेतिः Praheti, च and, भ्रातरौ two brothers, राक्षसाधिपौ lords of Rākṣasas, मधुकैटभसङ्काशौ resembling Madhu and Kaiṭabha, बभूवतुः existed, अरिन्दमौ subduers of enemies.
explanation: There existed two demon lords, Heti and Praheti, who were brothers, vanquishers of foes, and resembled Madhu and Kaiṭabha.

shloka_text: प्रहेतिर्धार्मिकस्तत्र तपोवनगतस्तदा । हेतिर्दारक्रियार्थे तु परं यत्नमथाकरोत् ।। 7.4.15 ।।
transliteration: prahetirdhārmikastatra tapovanagatastadā | hetirdārakriyārthe tu paraṃ yatnamathākarot || 7.4.15 ||
translation: प्रहेतिः Praheti, धार्मिकः righteous, तत्र there, तपोवनगतः gone to a hermitage, तदा then, हेतिः Heti, दारक्रियार्थे for the purpose of marriage, तु but, परम् great, यत्नम् effort, अथ then, अकरोत् made.
explanation: At that time, Praheti, being righteous, went to a hermitage, while Heti made a great effort to find a wife.

shloka_text: स कालभगिनीं कन्यां भयां नाम भयावहाम् । उदावहदमेयात्मा स्वयमेव महामतिः ।। 7.4.16 ।।
transliteration: sa kālabhaginīṃ kanyāṃ bhayāṃ nāma bhayāvahām | udāvahadameyātmā svayameva mahāmatiḥ || 7.4.16 ||
translation: सः he, कालभगिनीम् sister of Kala, कन्याम् maiden, भयाम् Bhaya, नाम named, भयावहाम् terrifying, उदावहत married, अमेयात्मा of immeasurable spirit, स्वयम् himself, एव indeed, महामतिः great-minded.
explanation: That great-minded Heti, of immeasurable spirit, himself married a terrifying maiden named Bhaya, who was the sister of Kala (Death).

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः । पुत्रं पुत्रवतां श्रेष्ठो विद्युत्केश इति श्रुतम् ।। 7.4.17 ।।
transliteration: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa hetī rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ | putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭho vidyutkeśa iti śrutam || 7.4.17 ||
translation: सः he, तस्याम् in her, जनयामास begot, हेती Heti, राक्षसपुङ्गवः foremost among Rākṣasas, पुत्रम् a son, पुत्रवताम् among those who have sons, श्रेष्ठः best, विद्युत्केशः Vidyutkeśa, इति thus, श्रुतम् known.
explanation: Heti, the foremost among Rākṣasas and best among those with sons, begot a son named Vidyutkeśa in her (Bhaya).

shloka_text: विद्युत्केशो हेतिपुत्रः स दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः । व्यवर्धत महातेजास्तोयमध्य इवाम्बुदः ।। 7.4.18 ।।
transliteration: vidyutkeśo hetiputraḥ sa dīptārkasamaprabhaḥ | vyavardhata mahātejāstoyamadhya ivāmbudaḥ || 7.4.18 ||
translation: विद्युत्केशः Vidyutkeśa, हेतिपुत्रः Heti's son, सः he, दीप्तार्कसमप्रभः having a brilliance equal to the blazing sun, व्यवर्धत grew, महातेजाः of great splendor, तोयमध्ये in the midst of water, इव like, अम्बुदः a cloud.
explanation: Vidyutkeśa, Heti's son, of great splendor and brilliance like the blazing sun, grew like a cloud in the midst of water.

shloka_text: स यदा यौवनं भद्रमनुप्राप्तो निशाचरः । ततो दारक्रियां तस्य कर्तुं व्यवसितः पिता ।। 7.4.19 ।।
transliteration: sa yadā yauvanaṃ bhadramanuprāpto niśācaraḥ | tato dārakriyāṃ tasya kartuṃ vyavasitaḥ pitā || 7.4.19 ||
translation: सः he, यदा when, यौवनम् youth, भद्रम् auspicious, अनुप्राप्तः attained, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, ततः then, दारक्रियाम् marriage ceremony, तस्य his, कर्तुम् to perform, व्यवसितः resolved, पिता father.
explanation: When the night-wanderer (Vidhyutkesha) attained auspicious youth, his father then resolved to perform his marriage ceremony.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां सो ऽथ सन्ध्यातुल्यां प्रभावतः । वरयामास पुत्रार्थं हेती राक्षसपुङ्गवः ।। 7.4.20 ।।
transliteration: sandhyāyāstanayāṃ so 'tha sandhyātulyāṃ prabhāvataḥ | varayāmāsa putrārthaṃ hetī rākṣasapuṅgavaḥ || 7.4.20 ||
translation: सन्ध्यायाः of Sandhya, तनयाम् daughter, सः he, अथ then, सन्ध्यातुल्याम् equal to Sandhya, प्रभावतः in splendor, वरयामास sought as a bride, पुत्रार्थम् for his son, हेती Heti, राक्षसपुङ्गवः the chief of Rakshasas.
explanation: Then Heti, the chief of Rakshasas, sought Sandhya's daughter, who was equal to Sandhya in splendor, as a bride for his son.

shloka_text: अवश्यमेव दातव्या परस्मै सेति सन्ध्यया । चिन्तयित्वा सुता दत्ता विद्युत्केशाय राघव ।। 7.4.21 ।।
transliteration: avaśyameva dātavyā parasmai seti sandhyayā | cintayitvā sutā dattā vidyutkeśāya rāghava || 7.4.21 ||
translation: अवश्यम् certainly, एव indeed, दातव्या to be given, परस्मै to another, सा she, इति thus, सन्ध्यया by Sandhya, चिन्तयित्वा having thought, सुता the daughter, दत्ता was given, विद्युत्केशाय to Vidhyutkesha, राघव O Rama.
explanation: O Rama, Sandhya, having thought that her daughter must certainly be given to another, thus gave her daughter to Vidhyutkesha.

shloka_text: सन्ध्यायास्तनयां लब्ध्वा विद्युत्केशो निशाचरः । रमते स्म तया सार्धं पौलोम्या मघवानिव ।। 7.4.22 ।।
transliteration: sandhyāyāstanayāṃ labdhvā vidyutkeśo niśācaraḥ | ramate sma tayā sārdhaṃ paulomyā maghavāniva || 7.4.22 ||
translation: सन्ध्यायाः of Sandhya, तनयाम् daughter, लब्ध्वा having obtained, विद्युत्केशः Vidhyutkesha, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, रमते स्म enjoyed, तया with her, सार्धम् together, पौलोम्या with Paulomi, मघवानिव like Maghavan.
explanation: Having obtained Sandhya's daughter, the night-wanderer Vidhyutkesha enjoyed with her, just as Maghavan (Indra) enjoys with Paulomi.

shloka_text: केनचित्त्वथ कालेन राम सालकटङ्कटा । विद्युत्केशाद्गर्भमाप घनराजिरिवार्णवात् ।। 7.4.23 ।।
transliteration: kenacittvatha kālena rāma sālakaṭaṅkaṭā | vidyutkeśādgarbhamāpa ghanarājirivārṇavāt || 7.4.23 ||
translation: केनचित् by some, तु indeed, अथ then, कालेन by time, राम O Rama, सालकटङ्कटा Salakatankata, विद्युत्केशात् from Vidhyutkesha, गर्भम् conception, आप obtained, घनराजिः a line of clouds, इव like, अर्णवात् from the ocean.
explanation: O Rama, after some time, Salakatankata conceived from Vidhyutkesha, just as a line of clouds obtains moisture from the ocean.

shloka_text: ततः सा राक्षसी गर्भं घनगर्भसमप्रभम् । प्रसूता मन्दरं गत्वा गङ्गा गर्भमिवाग्निजम् ।। 7.4.24 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā rākṣasī garbhaṃ ghanagarbhasamaprabham | prasūtā mandaraṃ gatvā gaṅgā garbhamivāgnijam || 7.4.24 ||
translation: ततः then, सा that, राक्षसी female demon, गर्भं offspring, घनगर्भसमप्रभम् having the luster like a thundercloud, प्रसूता gave birth, मन्दरं to Mandara mountain, गत्वा having gone, गङ्गा Ganga, गर्भमिव like an embryo, अग्निजम् born of fire.
explanation: Then, that female demon, having gone to the Mandara mountain, gave birth to an offspring shining like a thundercloud, just as Ganga gave birth to the fire-born embryo (Kartikeya).

shloka_text: समुत्सृज्य तु सा गर्भं विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी । रेमे तु सार्धं पतिना विस्मृत्य सुतमात्मजम् ।। 7.4.25 ।।
transliteration: samutsṛjya tu sā garbhaṃ vidyutkeśaratārthinī | reme tu sārdhaṃ patinā vismṛtya sutamātmajam || 7.4.25 ||
translation: समुत्सृज्य having abandoned, तु indeed, सा she, गर्भं the offspring, विद्युत्केशरतार्थिनी desiring union with Vidyutkesha, रेमे enjoyed, तु indeed, सार्धं with, पतिना her husband, विस्मृत्य having forgotten, सुतम् the son, आत्मजम् her own.
explanation: Having abandoned her offspring, she, desiring union with Vidyutkesha, then enjoyed herself with her husband, completely forgetting her own son.

shloka_text: उत्सृष्टस्तु तदा गर्भो घनशब्दसमस्वनः । तयोत्सृष्टः स तु शिशुः शरदर्कसमद्युतिः । निधायास्ये स्वयं मुष्टिं रुरोद शनकैस्तदा ।। 7.4.26 ।।
transliteration: utsṛṣṭastu tadā garbho ghanaśabdasamasvanaḥ | tayotsṛṣṭaḥ sa tu śiśuḥ śaradarkasamadyutiḥ | nidhāyāsye svayaṃ muṣṭiṃ ruroda śanakaistadā || 7.4.26 ||
translation: उत्सृष्टस्तु but abandoned, तदा then, गर्भो the offspring, घनशब्दसमस्वनः having a sound like the roar of a cloud, तयोत्सृष्टः abandoned by her, स that, तु indeed, शिशुः child, शरदर्कसमद्युतिः having the luster like the autumn sun, निधायास्ये having placed in his mouth, स्वयं himself, मुष्टिं a fist, रुरोद cried, शनकैस्तदा slowly then.
explanation: The abandoned offspring, who had a roar like thunder and a luster like the autumn sun, then cried slowly, having placed his own fist in his mouth.

shloka_text: ततो वृषभमास्थाय पार्वत्या सहितः शिवः । वायुमार्गेण गच्छन्वै शुश्राव रुदितस्वनम् ।। 7.4.27 ।।
transliteration: tato vṛṣabhamāsthāya pārvatyā sahitaḥ śivaḥ | vāyumārgeṇa gacchanvai śuśrāva ruditasvanam || 7.4.27 ||
translation: ततो then, वृषभम् a bull, आस्थाय having mounted, पार्वत्या with Parvati, सहितः accompanied, शिवः Shiva, वायुमार्गेण through the sky-path, गच्छन्वै indeed going, शुश्राव heard, रुदितस्वनम् the sound of crying.
explanation: Then Shiva, accompanied by Parvati and mounted on a bull, was traveling through the sky and heard the sound of crying.

shloka_text: अपश्यदुमया सार्धं रुदन्तं राक्षसात्मजम् । कारुण्यभावात्पार्वत्या भवस्त्रिपुरसूदनः ।। 7.4.28 ।।
transliteration: apaśyadumayā sārdhaṃ rudantaṃ rākṣasātmajam | kāruṇyabhāvātpārvatyā bhavastripurasūdanaḥ || 7.4.28 ||
translation: अपश्यत् he saw, उमया with Uma, सार्धं together, रुदन्तं crying, राक्षसात्मजम् the demon's son, कारुण्यभावात् due to the feeling of compassion, पार्वत्या of Parvati, भवः Shiva, त्रिपुरसूदनः the destroyer of Tripura.
explanation: Shiva, the destroyer of Tripura, then saw the demon's son crying, accompanied by Uma, moved by Parvati's feeling of compassion.

shloka_text: तं राक्षसात्मजं चक्रे मातुरेव वयःसमम् । अमरं चैव तं कृत्वा महादेवो ऽक्षरो ऽव्ययः ।। 7.4.29 ।।
transliteration: taṃ rākṣasātmajaṃ cakre mātureva vayaḥsamam | amaraṃ caiva taṃ kṛtvā mahādevo 'kṣaro 'vyayaḥ || 7.4.29 ||
translation: तं him, राक्षसात्मजं the son of the demon, चक्रे made, मातुरेव of his mother only, वयःसमम् equal in age, अमरं immortal, चैव and indeed, तं him, कृत्वा having made, महादेवो Lord Mahadeva, अक्षरो imperishable, अव्ययः immutable.
explanation: The imperishable and immutable Lord Mahadeva made that son of the demon, Sukesha, immortal and equal in age to his mother.

shloka_text: पुरमाकाशगं प्रादात्पार्वत्याः प्रियकाम्यया । उमयापि वरो दत्तो राक्षसानां नृपात्मज ।। 7.4.30 ।।
transliteration: puramākāśagaṃ prādātpārvatyāḥ priyakāmyayā | umayāpi varo datto rākṣasānāṃ nṛpātmaja || 7.4.30 ||
translation: पुरम् a city, आकाशगं moving in the sky, प्रादात् gave, पार्वत्याः of Parvati, प्रियकाम्यया with the desire to please, उमयापि by Uma also, वरो a boon, दत्तो given, राक्षसानां to the demons, नृपात्मज O son of the king.
explanation: To please Parvati, Shiva gave him a city that could move in the sky, and O son of the king, Uma also granted a boon to the demons.

shloka_text: सद्योपलब्धिर्गर्भस्य प्रसूतिः सद्य एव च । सद्य एव वयःप्राप्तिर्मातुरेव वयस्समम् ।। 7.4.31 ।।
transliteration: sadyopalabdhirgarbhasya prasūtiḥ sadya eva ca | sadya eva vayaḥprāptirmātureva vayassamam || 7.4.31 ||
translation: सद्योपलब्धिः immediate conception, गर्भस्य of the embryo, प्रसूतिः birth, सद्य immediately, एव indeed, च and, सद्य immediately, एव indeed, वयःप्राप्तिः attainment of age, मातुरेव of the mother only, वयस्समम् equal in age.
explanation: The boon granted by Uma was that conception would be immediate, birth would be immediate, and the child would immediately attain an age equal to that of its mother.

shloka_text: ततः सुकेशो वरदानगर्वितः श्रियं प्रभोः प्राप्य हरस्य पार्श्वतः । चचार सर्वत्र महान्महामतिः खगं पुरं प्राप्य पुरन्दरो यथा ।। 7.4.32 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sukeśo varadānagarvitaḥ śriyaṃ prabhoḥ prāpya harasya pārśvataḥ | cacāra sarvatra mahānmahāmatiḥ khagaṃ puraṃ prāpya purandaro yathā || 7.4.32 ||
translation: ततः then, सुकेशो Sukesha, वरदानगर्वितः proud of the boon, श्रियं glory, प्रभोः of the lord, प्राप्य having obtained, हरस्य of Shiva, पार्श्वतः from the presence, चचार roamed, सर्वत्र everywhere, महान् great, महामतिः of great intellect, खगं moving in the sky, पुरं city, प्राप्य having obtained, पुरन्दरो Indra, यथा just as.
explanation: Then, Sukesha, proud of the boon and having obtained glory from the presence of Lord Shiva, roamed everywhere, great and of great intellect, just as Indra does after obtaining his celestial city. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः ।। 4 ।। Thus ends the fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
